transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
I’m here because I can’t shake this feeling that work isn’t safe anymore. And I keep thinking I’m damaged somehow—like the capable person who got promoted isn’t really there anymore.
Did something happen at work that felt traumatic or terrifying to you?

Yes. A badge scanner beeping, heavy footsteps in the hallway, even a late-night deployment alert can suddenly put me right back in that office. My chest gets tight, and I see the guard on the floor like it’s cutting into whatever I’m doing.
Do you go out of your way to avoid things that remind you of what happened at work?

Yeah. I’ve been trading shifts and pushing back on release windows when I can. I take the side entrance, or work from home, because going through that lobby after dark… I feel like I’m going to come apart.
Since this happened, have you been feeling constantly on guard or easily startled?

Yes. I’m always scanning things without meaning to. On the train, in meetings, even at lunch, I’m clocking the exits and noticing who’s standing too close. I keep listening for noises in the hallway instead of really being present.
Since this happened, have you been feeling persistently negative about yourself, other people, or the world?
Yes. I keep thinking work just isn’t safe anymore. And... I don’t feel like myself there. Like the capable person who got promoted is gone somehow, or damaged.
Do you ever feel as if the event at work is happening again in the moment?

Yes. A badge scanner beeping, heavy footsteps in the hallway, or a late-night deployment alert can just put me right back in that office. My chest gets tight, and I see the guard on the floor like it’s happening again.
How long have these symptoms been going on since the incident at work?
Since the break-in during that overnight deployment—about two years and four months now.
Have these symptoms made it hard for you to do your job?

Yes. My work has slipped. I’ve missed migration deadlines and avoided some of the late deployments that are important. I got called out in a performance review for conflicts that never used to happen. And I’ve pulled back from mentoring and the women-in-tech leadership events—I just don’t feel steady or reliable enough anymore.
Are there important parts of the break-in that you still cannot remember?

I remember hiding, and I remember the police being there afterward. But the part where they came into the conference room and got me out is just… blank. I try to remember it, but it feels like that part of the memory is corrupted.
